name: Lake Ann Approach Scramble
approach: From the Austin Pass/Artist Point trailhead (paved lot at the end of SR 542, roughly 58 miles / 1.5-2 hr from Bellingham), follow the signed Lake Ann Trail #600, which drops about 800 ft into the Swift Creek headwaters basin before climbing back up past Lake Ann (4.1 miles one-way to the lake area) to a 4,900-ft saddle northwest of the lake. From the saddle, leave the maintained trail for a boot path heading southwest then south along the ridge crest; where the ridge steepens near 5,300 ft the path contours the east side before the crest re-forms — follow cairns over Peak 5681 and scramble roughly 0.5 mile west along the summit ridge to Mount Ann. Total round trip is about 10.5 miles with roughly 4,000 ft of cumulative elevation gain.

approach_variants.name: Lake Ann Trail #600 to the 4,900 ft saddle, then the boot path and cairns over Peak 5681
approach_variants.notes:
From the Austin Pass / Artist Point trailhead at the end of SR-542, follow the signed Lake Ann Trail #600. It drops about 800 ft into the Swift Creek headwaters basin before climbing back up past Lake Ann — 4.1 miles one way to the lake area — to a saddle at 4,900 ft northwest of the lake.

From the saddle, leave the maintained trail for a boot path heading southwest then south along the ridge crest. Where the ridge steepens near 5,300 ft the path contours the east side before the crest re-forms; from there follow cairns over Peak 5681 and scramble roughly half a mile west along the summit ridge to Mount Ann.

About 10.5 miles round trip with roughly 4,000 ft of cumulative gain, part of which comes from the fact that the trail loses 800 ft at the start and you pay it back at the end.

Note on the name: this is the Lake Ann below Artist Point on SR-542, not the Lake Ann near Maple Pass. One route has already been recorded with the wrong Lake Ann's trailhead.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Jul-Sep snow-free; winter and spring ascents are done by experienced parties with mountaineering gear on a stable snowpack
hazards: Cairns as the only navigation above 5,300 ft, in both directions
Contouring low on the return, which cliffs out above the Swift Creek basin
An 800 ft descent at the start that must be re-climbed at the end of the day
Two Lake Anns in the North Cascades, and one of them has already been given the wrong trailhead
Lingering snow on the traverse in early season
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The 4,900 ft saddle northwest of the lake is where the route starts, and it is the last piece of maintained trail. Below it, built tread. Above it, a boot path. If you are still on graded trail heading toward the Fisher Chimneys and Shuksan, you have walked past your turn — that is the same trail, continuing.

The bearing out of the saddle is southwest, then south, along the crest. Two headings in sequence. In cloud, keep the crest under your feet.

The one place the route leaves the crest is near 5,300 ft, and it goes east. Where the ridge steepens the path contours the east side before the crest re-forms above. Contouring west here puts you on the wrong side of the ridge above the Swift Creek basin.

Cairns are the handrail above 5,300 ft, and losing them is the main route-finding hazard in poor visibility, in both directions. Note them going up.

Arrival: the scrambling ridge runs roughly half a mile west from Peak 5681 to Mount Ann's summit. Peak 5681 is not the top — if you are standing on a high point and there is more ridge running west, keep going.

And the return trap, which is worth stating because it is a cliff problem rather than a navigation one: coming back, stay high on the ridge rather than contouring low where the path is indistinct. Contouring low here cliffs out above the basin.

waypoints.name: Lake Ann Trailhead (Austin Pass)
waypoints.note: Paved lot on SR 542 just below Artist Point; Northwest Forest Pass required, overnight parties sign the trailhead register (no camping permit needed).
waypoints.directions: Drive Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) to its end at the Austin Pass/Artist Point trailhead, a paved lot roughly 58 miles and 1.5-2 hours from Bellingham. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and overnight parties sign the wilderness register at the trailhead; no camping permit is needed. The upper highway to Austin Pass typically doesn't open until late June or early July, depending on snowpack, and the trailhead has had weekend-focused access in recent seasons, so check current alerts before planning a start time.

waypoints.name: Swift Creek Trail 607 junction
waypoints.note: Trail drops ~800 ft from the trailhead into the Swift Creek headwaters basin; Swift Creek Trail splits off here, stay on Lake Ann Trail 600.

waypoints.name: Swift Creek meadow crossing
waypoints.note: Trail bottoms out through a wildflower meadow alongside upper Swift Creek before climbing again; reliable water but snowfields can bury the crossing into August.

waypoints.name: Lake Ann
waypoints.note: Established camp basin below Mount Shuksan's Fisher Chimneys; must camp at least 2 mi from trailhead, and it fills up on weekends.

waypoints.name: 4,900-ft saddle NW of Lake Ann
waypoints.note: Leave the maintained trail here; a boot path heads southwest then south along the ridge toward Peak 5681 — this is the scramble jump-off point.

waypoints.name: Ridge steepening / indistinct boot path
waypoints.note: Path contours the east side of the ridge and gets hard to follow above ~5,300 ft; stay high on the ridge crest and watch for cairns rather than dropping onto loose east-facing slopes.

waypoints.name: Peak 5681 (Han Peak/Mount Annette)
waypoints.note: Tree-covered subsidiary summit on the connecting ridge; from here continue west along an up-and-down ridge crest (steeper than it looks on the topo) toward Mount Ann.

waypoints.name: Mount Ann summit
waypoints.note: True summit, ~0.5 mi west of Peak 5681 along the ridge; Class 2-3 scrambling on the final pitch with views of Mount Shuksan and Mount Baker.
